rankings.reason: Sign flips at the 2D horizon (loose: -0.201%, tight: -0.125%) before turning positive at 3D/5D; neither symbol- nor day-cluster bootstrap excludes zero at ANY of its 6 cells despite 351-903 trades per cell -- statistically indistinguishable from noise despite decent sample size.
Uniformly negative across all 12 cells (both bands, all 3 horizons, both LONG and SHORT sub-legs) -- a clean, unambiguous rejection, the mechanical mirror-image of the REVERSAL finding.

The larger, more reliable loose-band cells (63 trades/30 symbols/44 days) show gross expectancy near zero and NEGATIVE net expectancy after 10bps cost (-0.025% to -0.052%). The tight-band cells show a small positive net (+0.017% to +0.170%) but on only 25 trades/17 symbols/19-23 days -- too thin to independently corroborate, not treated as a separate finding.

Attractive point estimates (net@10bps +0.148% to +0.552%) but n=25-48 trades per cell, and BOTH symbol- and day-cluster bootstrap CIs cross zero at EVERY one of the 4 cells. Per-regime trade counts are 3-8 -- far too thin to assess regime stability meaningfully. This is exactly the small-sample pattern the program's own forensic history (Task71's failure_forensics.md) warns against rewarding.
Feasibility-only; no defensible point-in-time universe/liquidity data source exists in this repo (see universe_expansion_feasibility.json). Zero outcome cells.
